title: A Escarpment for the Landfall
premise: Ivo Ashgrove, a riverboat captain hiding from a past conviction she never deserved, discovers a tide-revealed cave holding the drowned archive of the Corvane family, who have ruled the river valley for generations by erasing their crimes from every record. The compass she inherited points not north but toward the river's forbidden source, where the original ledger of Corvane sins is kept—and where her father died trying to reach it. Hunted by the family's enforcer and shadowed by a debt collector who may be an ally in disguise, Ivo runs the gauntlet upstream through flooded towns, bribed locks, and loyalists of a forgotten rebellion. At the source, she must choose between destroying the archive to free the valley or using its power herself; she chooses to broadcast it to every riverside town at once, breaking the Corvanes' monopoly on memory, though it costs her the boat, the cave, and any hope of returning to invisibility.
about_author: Oscar Sandoval is a former barge hand who spent eleven years working the inland waterways before turning to writing full-time. His fiction draws on the river towns' oral histories and his fascination with what powerful families prefer forgotten.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A routine run down the Vell River establishes Ivo's skill, her debt to the Harrow Syndicate, and her careful anonymity—she pays cash, uses no surname, keeps no photographs. When a syndicate man boards demanding faster repayment, the beat is quiet dread: her invisible life is already fraying.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. An extreme low tide exposes a sea cave below the cliffs at Landfall Point. Inside she finds a sealed chamber of documents, portraits, and a brass compass engraved with her family name. The emotional beat is vertigo: the past she buried has been waiting for her.

chapters.title: Admission Charged by Legend
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, brief interlude from tavern-keeper Maren. Locals tell half-joking legends of the Corvane Archive; Maren recognizes Ivo's face from an old wanted notice and says nothing—but someone else was asking about the cave last week. Beat: Ivo realizes she is being hunted before she even understands what she holds.

chapters.title: The Man Who Collects
chapters.summary: Debt collector Silas Fen's POV. Fen boards Ivo's boat ostensibly for payment but is really assessing whether she found the cave—he works for the Corvanes as much as the Syndicate. His chapters reveal he keeps his own secret ledger of the family's crimes. Beat: ambiguous menace with a flicker of sympathy.

chapters.title: Compass Points Upstream
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The compass needle ignores north and swings steadily upriver. Cross-referencing the cave documents, Ivo learns her father reached the source twenty years ago and never came back, branded a thief for it. Beat: grief converted into resolve—she will follow the river to its head.

chapters.title: Lock Nine Takes Its Toll
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At Lock Nine, Corvane agents inspect every vessel. Ivo hides the documents inside her ballast and talks her way through by flattering the lockmaster's vanity. First direct contact with the enemy; beat: adrenaline and the discovery that fear sharpens rather than paralyzes her.

chapters.title: The Drowned Parish
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She shelters in a town half-sunk by a Corvane dam project that displaced thousands and erased the event from official maps. An old woman recognizes the compass as belonging to 'the mapmaker's daughter.' Beat: Ivo understands the stakes are bigger than her name—it's everyone's erased history.

chapters.title: Fen Catches the Current
chapters.summary: Silas Fen's POV. Fen trails Ivo upstream, sabotaging her permits while quietly leaving her fuel where she'll find it. His internal conflict deepens: his brother died in the drowned parish. Beat: the hunter begins keeping two ledgers—one for his employers, one for himself.

chapters.title: A Rebellion Nobody Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the hills above the river she finds survivors of the Millwright Uprising, crushed decades ago, who recognize the archive seal. Their leader, Odile, tests Ivo's motives harshly. Beat: wary alliance—Ivo gains guides and safehouses, and learns the source is guarded.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The Syndicate catches up; they seize her boat as collateral and give her three days. Stripped of her vessel, Ivo must travel overland with only the compass and Odile's mule track. Beat: loss and humility—the river girl learns to walk.

chapters.title: What Odile Buried
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reveals she helped Ivo's father on his final journey and abandoned him at the gorge when Corvane riders came; her guilt has calcified into doctrine: never touch the source again. Beat: betrayal confessed, trust nearly shattered, then grudgingly rebuilt.

chapters.title: High Water at Hallowford
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Corvane forces flood the valley road to trap her; Fen, ordered to capture her, instead cuts the sluice gates to open an escape channel, openly defecting. Beat: spectacular set piece—Fen's choice made public, both now outlaws together.

chapters.title: Two Ledgers
chapters.summary: Alternating Ivo/Fen POV around a fire. They compare notes: Fen's records corroborate the archive, and together the evidence becomes undeniable. But Ivo admits a temptation—if she controlled the archive, no one could ever hurt her again. Beat: the theme of corruption surfaces inside the heroine herself.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The party reaches the gorge where her father turned back. Carved into the walls are names of the disappeared—including ASHGROVE. Ivo finds her father's final message scratched beside it: the source remembers everything. Beat: mourning transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: Wardens of the Source
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the river's headwaters stands a fortified station where Corvane archivists curate reality itself—deciding which floods, famines, and massacres enter the record. Ivo infiltrates disguised as a supply clerk. Beat: cold horror; power revealed not as violence but as editing.

chapters.title: The Reading Room
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Deep in the vault she finds the master ledger and, unexpectedly, the Archivist—a dying old woman who has kept the truth safe inside the machine meant to destroy it, waiting for someone with 'the compass and the grudge.' Beat: revelation and passing of the torch.

chapters.title: Corvane Comes Upstream
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Patriarch Edmun Corvane arrives with riders to burn the vault and everything in it, including Ivo. He offers her a bargain: her father's name cleared, her debt dissolved, in exchange for silence. Beat: the devil's offer, genuinely tempting, refused.

chapters.title: Everything the River Carries
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The climax: rather than destroy or hoard the ledger, Ivo and Fen load it onto the Corvane mail steamer and release copies at every lock and landing downstream via the river's own current and couriers. Corvane riders pursue; Odile holds the gorge. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, the boat burning.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs across one day: towns along the river read their true histories aloud in markets and churches. Edmun Corvane's authority dissolves not in battle but in embarrassment and mass refusal. Beat: catharsis—justice arriving not through law but through shared memory.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Account
chapters.summary: Silas Fen's POV. Fen settles accounts: he burns the Syndicate's claim against Ivo, testifies to a newly convened river tribunal, and accepts his own reckoning for years of complicity. Beat: accountability modeled—justice outside the law still demands a price.

chapters.title: A New Chart
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Months later, Ivo pilots a modest ferry under her real name for the first time since her conviction was overturned. The cave is sealed by common consent—not hidden, just finished with. Beat: peace earned, identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Where the Water Begins
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ivo's POV. She hikes once more to the source, leaves her father's compass there among the carved names, and watches the first clean water gather. Closing beat: memory as a living spring—powerless to corrupt because it belongs to everyone now.
